internal_refs.relationship: §12940 provides the substantive FEHA violations; §12965 provides the exclusive procedural pathway to litigate them
§132a has independent 1-year WCAB SOL — runs concurrently with FEHA §12965 pathway; must be monitored separately
§1102.5 whistleblower has 3-year Superior Court SOL; no CRD exhaustion required — unlike FEHA §12965

external_refs.relationship: Concurrent EEOC filing under ADA/Title VII triggers §12965(e)+(f) tolling of FEHA SOL — coordinate federal and state tracks
FEHA civil action in Superior Court — discovery, pleading, summary judgment standards governed by CCP; coordinate with civil litigation framework

case_law.citation: City of Moorpark v. Superior Court, 18 Cal.4th 1143 (1998)
case_law.holding: FEHA civil actions may recover full back pay, front pay, emotional distress, and punitive damages; not limited to contract damages
case_law.significance: Confirmed full damages available in §12965 civil actions

case_law.citation: Romano v. Rockwell International, Inc., 14 Cal.4th 479 (1996)
case_law.holding: §12965 right-to-sue SOL is subject to equitable tolling; discovery rule applies where discriminatory act was concealed
case_law.significance: Established equitable tolling for concealed discrimination — critical for identity replacement cases where false designation was not disclosed to worker
